one_month_reasoning: The one scheduled company event in the window is Q3 2026 results, expected after the close on 2026-10-26 (source 12; Cadence has not yet announced the webcast). Guidance is Q3 revenue of $1.595-1.625B and non-GAAP EPS of $2.01-2.07 (source 2), and consensus sits near the midpoint (source 10). Cadence beat the top of its EPS guidance in Q2 ($2.11 vs $2.02-2.08, sources 2 and 4) and raised FY revenue guidance in both Q1 and Q2 while holding the FY EPS range at $8.05-8.15 (sources 4, 15). So a small beat and a modest revenue raise are the most likely outcome, but H2 margins are guided lower for Hexagon integration spend (source 5). Corrected price path from the daily series (source 22): the stock fell from $340 on Aug 31 to $273.96 on Sept 15 with no company news (yields and valuation), then rallied 28% in 12 sessions to $350.75. That includes +6.2% on Oct 1 on the Synopsys investor-day read-through (FY27 +15% guide, source 21) and a Morgan Stanley target raise to $400 (source 23). After a move that sharp, short-term reversal risk roughly offsets the beat-and-raise drift. The BIS affiliates-rule date has moved out of the window: the truce extension to Jan 10, 2027 pushes it past Nov 9 (source 24). I therefore use a near-symmetric lognormal with a median of about $351 and a 1-month sigma of about 12.5%. That is a little above annual vol / 3.5 (11.7%) to allow for the earnings gap and the recent volatility.

fair_value.method: Blend of 60% P/E (FY2028E non-GAAP EPS $10.90 x 36x = $392) and 40% FCF yield (FY2028E FCF $2.4B at 2.5% = $96B, ~zero net debt by Oct-2027, 276M diluted shares = $348). That gives ~$375 at Oct-2027, unchanged from the capped run because the verified inputs moved in offsetting directions: more shares, less net debt.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY2028E non-GAAP EPS $10.90 (NTM at Oct-2027) x 36x forward multiple

inputs_detail.derivation: Zacks shows $9.43 (source 10). I cross-check bottom-up: $7.16B revenue x ~45% non-GAAP margin (FY2025 was 44.6%, FY2026 guide 44.25%, and management says 2027 margins improve, sources 2 and 5), less ~$0.1B non-GAAP other expense, at the ~16.5% non-GAAP tax rate implied by the guide, over 276M shares = ~$9.45. I round to $9.50.

FY2027 $9.50 grown ~15%: revenue +12% to ~$8.0B and the margin up ~1pt to ~46%, with a flat share count. Support: the 10-Q says 58% of RPO (ex non-cancelable) converts within 12 months and 40% in months 13-36 (source 3). Next-12-month RPO rose from $3.8B at YE2025 to $4.2B at Q2 (sources 15, 2). Synopsys guides FY27 +15% and a 13%+ long-term EDA CAGR (source 21), which supports low-teens EDA demand.

FY2026 is guided at 275.5-277.5M, Q2 was 276.2M, and 3.2M shares were issued for Hexagon (source 3). Buybacks of ~$200M a quarter retire ~0.6M shares a quarter (source 2), which roughly offsets SBC issuance; the plan pool was raised by 5M shares (source 16). I therefore hold the count flat rather than shrinking it 1M a year as in the capped run.

$350.73 is ~36.9x FY2027E $9.50 and ~43x FY2026E, and the 5-year forward average is ~45x (source 11). The stock traded at ~29x FY2027E on Sept 15 with no fundamental news (source 22), which shows that derating risk is real. Synopsys's raised FY27 and long-term targets (source 21) and the SemiWiki and industry view that the Kimi K3 demo was a 45nm toy (sources 8, 25) argue against further compression. Synopsys management also calls agents additive to license demand (source 20). On balance I hold today's ~36x.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY2028E FCF $2.4B / 2.5% yield = $96B; net debt ~$0 at Oct-2027; 276M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2025 FCF was $1.587B ($1.729B OCF less $142M capex) against non-GAAP NI of ~$1.95B ($7.14 x 273.3M), i.e. 81%. FY2026 guide is ~$1.76B against ~$2.24B, i.e. 79%.
FY2028E non-GAAP NI ~$3.0B ($10.90 x 276M) x ~80% conversion = ~$2.4B.

At Q2 2026 net debt was $1.06B ($2.50B of notes less $1.44B cash). Over the ~15 months to Oct-2027 FCF is ~$2.2B, and management uses ~50% for buybacks (source 2), so ~$1.1B is retained. The $500M 4.2% notes due Sept 10, 2027 are repaid or refinanced (source 3).

At $350.73 (~$97B market cap) the yield on FY2026E FCF is ~1.8% and on FY2027E (~$2.1B) is ~2.2%. I use 2.5% on forward FCF to allow for SBC (H1 SBC $285M, source 3) and the derating range seen in Sept (source 22).

bear.story: The AI-agent and open-source disruption narrative returns, or the initial FY2027 guide (Feb-2027) lands near ~10% growth: Cadence guided 2026 initially at 11-13% (source 15). Hardware digests, and US-China talks fail when the truce ends on Jan 10, 2027, so the affiliates rule bites (China was 15% of Q2 revenue). FY2027 EPS ~$9.0 at ~27x, close to the Sept-15 trough multiple.

base.story: Beat-and-raise continues. FY2027 is guided ~11-12% and ends ~13%, backlog stays above $8B, and margins expand as Hexagon integration ends. FY2028E EPS ~$10.9 at ~35x.

bull.story: Agent consumption pricing shows up in bookings (ChipStack, super agents), IP keeps growing 30%+, and hardware stays supply-constrained. EDA peer guidance (Synopsys FY27 +15%, mid-20s EPS growth) re-rates the group toward the ~42-45x 5-year average on FY2028E EPS of ~$11.3.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$250, under the $262.75 52-week low and well under the $273.96 Sept-15 close, would most likely mean a fundamental reset rather than noise. That reset could be an FY2027 guide below ~10% growth, backlog falling from $8.1B, evidence that agents compress license pricing, or China access removed by the affiliates rule after the Jan 10, 2027 truce expiry. The September selloff to ~$274 came from yields and valuation without any change to fundamentals, so a level only modestly below it is not by itself a break.

key_uncertainties: Whether AI agents with open-source EDA erode pricing, or whether consumption pricing (which both Cadence and Synopsys are pursuing) raises tool usage. No agent revenue has been disclosed yet
The FY2027 guide after Hexagon laps: consensus is +13.3% revenue, the initial guide is likely lower, and the stock's reaction to a conservative guide is uncertain
US-China: the truce ends Jan 10, 2027 and the affiliates rule could be reimposed after that. China was 15% of Q2 revenue on an easy 2025 comparison
Hardware (Palladium/Protium) lumpiness and the AI capex cycle
Multiple: the stock swung between ~29x and ~37x FY2027E within three weeks in September, so the rate environment matters
reasoning: The continuation research verified the capped run's core numbers from primary filings and corrected several facts. Verified: Q2 revenue $1.584B (+24%), 45.5% non-GAAP margin, record $8.1B backlog, next-12-month RPO $4.2B (up from $3.8B at YE2025), FY2026 guide $6.26-6.34B and EPS $8.05-8.15, the 58%/40% RPO conversion footnote, net debt ~$1.06B, and no 10% customer. Corrections: (1) The FY2026 EPS guide has never been raised; it was $8.05-8.15 in February. The revenue raises (from $5.9-6.0B) include ~4pts from Hexagon, and the margin guide fell from 45.25% to 44.25% midpoint. So organic momentum is strong but EPS upside has been absorbed. (2) Diluted shares are ~276M, not 274M: 3.2M Hexagon shares, and buybacks only offset SBC. (3) The September low was $273.96 on Sept 15 with no news, not $293-320 after the July Kimi K3 scare. The stock then rose 28% to $350.75, helped on Oct 1 by Synopsys guiding FY27 +15% at its investor day and a Morgan Stanley target raise. (4) The BIS affiliates-rule suspension, which ran to Nov 9, 2026, was reportedly pushed to Jan 10, 2027 by the Sept-24 truce extension. Bull evidence I had not chased: Synopsys organic EDA expects double digits, guides FY27 +15%, and raised long-term targets. Both EDA leaders describe agents as subscription plus consumption. The TSMC A14/A16 certification and the ChipStack early deployments at NVIDIA and Qualcomm help, and the CEO's September Form 4s were tax withholding, not discretionary sales. Bear evidence: the multiple's sensitivity to rates (a 19% drop in two weeks in September), flat EPS guidance despite revenue raises, and China timing. Valuation: P/E $392 (60%) and FCF yield $348 (40%) give a fair value of ~$375, unchanged. Scenarios: bear $240 / base $380 / bull $490 at 22/52/26 (previously 25/50/25), mean ~$378. The bear weight is trimmed for the China deferral and the peer data. For the ladder I use a lognormal with a median of ~$370 and sigma ~0.35, below the 41% realized vol, which includes two narrative shocks, and with a slightly fattened far-left tail. P(>= today) is ~0.56. Twelve Data estimates and targets were plan-gated and Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, so consensus comes from Zacks and StockStory via web. No option-market data was consulted, and nothing under valuation/priors/ was opened.
